text.approach_logistics: {"trailhead":"Ossa Mountain trailhead, about 30 minutes from Squamish"}
text.overview: Ossa Mountain is climbed by its east ridge, a long day from the Squamish side with steep forest, meadows and creek crossings below a route-finding scramble. Near the top the route downclimbs into a notch and works through a chimney section before the summit.
text.descent: Return the same way; the downclimbs and loose ground make the descent as serious as the ascent.

earlierPasses.notes: Lead only, not proof: VOC wiki says the Ossa approach is the Sigurd Creek trail, leaving the spur road just past the Ashlu Creek bridge (Ashlu Creek Road off the Squamish River road), but that page describes the WEST ridge, not this east ridge, gives no parking spot and no coordinates. The stored text 'Ossa Mountain trailhead ~30 min from Squamish' comes from the FKT page, which also names no trailhead. No official candidates. BCMC and Steven Song pages did not yield the trailhead (Song page body not readable via WebFetch). Not guessed.

earlierPasses.notes: Three climber.org reports plus the climber.org driving page agree the documented start is Frenchman Lake / Spring Creek road (west side), but it is a forest-road walk with a snow-dependent start and no named trailhead; 'Standard route' does not say west or east and the register shows east-side (US 395) ascents too. Climber.org GPX waypoints for reference only, none is a trailhead: SPRJCT Spring Creek multi-road junction 39.89512,-120.14438; SPRCK4 'left car here in April' 39.90509,-120.13935; summit ADAMSP 39.91073,-120.10022. Summitpost east-side page gave 403. Left stuck rather than pin a road junction as a trailhead.

text.description: A remote peak reached off the John Muir Trail near Muir Pass; leave the trail for Black Giant Pass, then walk up about half a mile of loose rock to the summit. The east-side approach over Echo Col from Lake Sabrina adds class 3 and possible snow.

earlierPasses.notes: A backpack of 20+ miles with no single trailhead for 'west slope from Black Giant Pass'. Candidates: South Lake via Bishop Pass and Le Conte Canyon to the JMT and Muir Pass (USFS South Lake Trailhead 37.169305,-118.565813), Sabrina via Echo Col (the east variant the route text itself says adds class 3), or North Lake/Piute Pass. The only page about this pass I could open (climber.org 2006/1514) starts at Sabrina, i.e. the east variant. Route name and text put the line on the JMT side, which favours South Lake, but no page states it. Not guessed. Highsierratopix gave 403; Summitpost 403. Route reaches summit per its own text.

name: Via Summit Creek and Mosquito Pass

text.description: Follow Summit Creek trail about 10 miles to Lunch Meadow, leave the trail before Mosquito Pass, and climb a drainage to the summit ridge.

trailhead.name: Kennedy Meadows Trailhead (Summit Creek trail start)

identifiedBy.fact: trip report on this exact route: Summit Creek trail south 10 mi to Lunch Meadow, leave before Mosquito Pass; trailhead is the USFS trailhead off Hwy 108 near Kennedy Meadows Resort

placements.name: official trailhead of Relief Reservoir Trail

earlierPasses.notes: Strong: the 1999 report is the same route. The USFS campground point and the report's trailhead GPS agree within about 40 m. The stavislost point is about 0.9 km south, at the Relief Reservoir trail start; prefer the USFS / climber.org point. Do not use USFS 'Upper Kennedy Meadow Trailhead' 38.2996,-119.7404 (a different place about 2 km south). Peak is in the Emigrant Wilderness side of Kennedy Meadows although the stored path says Hoover Wilderness.

trailhead.name: Donner Summit / Boreal Ridge PCT trailhead (south parking area, Castle Peak Road exit)

identifiedBy.fact: Boreal Ridge / Castle Peak Road exit off I-80; parking north and south of freeway; PCT trailhead there; route text starts on the PCT under I-80 to Castle Pass

placements.name: DONERS Donner Pass south parking area

earlierPasses.notes: Moderate: the route text puts the start on the PCT passing under I-80, which is the PCT crossing at Boreal. The two placements agree within about 90 m. The north lot (DONERN 39.34100,-120.34748) is the other parking area. No page I read uses the words Castle Pass; the 2000 and 2009 reports climb the west ridge from this same snow park. Trailhead is 2.9 km from the summit pin.

earlierPasses.notes: Route's own text starts 'from a high camp' (Ionian Basin) and no trailhead. Documented trips use different starts: Lake Sabrina via Echo Col (one blog trip report, opened) and Courtwright/Wishon (SummitPost, not opened, blocked). Peak is a multi-day approach reachable from several trailheads (Sabrina, South Lake/Bishop Pass, Courtwright); no page says which one this route uses. Lake Sabrina (USFS SABRINA LAKE TH 37.213605,-118.610013) is a lead only, one trip report. SummitPost 403, climber.org report index not itemized.

identifiedBy.fact: Cross Kearsarge Pass, descend to Bubbs Creek (Kearsarge Pass trail starts at Onion Valley)

earlierPasses.notes: First pass missed that the text names Kearsarge Pass. Kearsarge Pass is reached only from Onion Valley on the east side (Onion Valley road end); the Kearsarge Pass trail from Onion Valley is documented on the Center Peak report (https://climber.org/reports/1998/311.html). Inference from the pass name, not a page about Deerhorn. A Kearsarge Pass entry from the west (Cedar Grove/Bubbs Creek) would not 'cross' it descending to Bubbs Creek, so Onion Valley is the consistent reading. One placement; USFS point is the campground, ~100 m from the road-end lot.
